summary: The stated fourth-root transport inequality and its arbitrary-good-cutoff and gate consequences are proved without a core-moment hypothesis. The Boolean input applies to the explicitly identified downsets, including the empty ground set, and retains ordered displacements and zero. The reflected endpoint energies, disjoint core-copy embeddings, exact original atom masses, and halfspace comparison are valid for all permitted cores, including r=0 and lower affine rank. Cubing the depth bound and sampling roots gives exactly four factors of the full normalizer Z. Selecting one threshold per label makes the sampled root sets disjoint. The energy-ordered stock comparison yields the exponent 9/8 without assuming monotonicity of the core moments; its series bound and Holder over 2^s labels give the stated constant. The marginal pi and retained mass alpha use the original combined law. Restriction to arbitrary good cutoffs and the gate identity are exact. The cases s=0, T=0, beta=0, empty good sets, tied energies, and both gate endpoints introduce no errors or gaps.
